summary: Kristina Myrvold specializes in religious studies and Indology. A Ph.D. candidate at Lund University (attested 2008), she worked there as an editor (attested 2005) and later became Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Linnaeus University (attested 2014).

Sinologist and religious studies scholar Kristofer Schipper studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1958–1962). He held posts at the EFEO (~1962–1970) and Leiden University (~1993–1999).

Krisztina Teleki works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1997–2009), earning an MA in Tibetan and Mongolian, and later served there as a research fellow.
Kshanika Saha worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a PhD from the University of Calcutta (attested 1966), where she studied under Nalinaksha Dutt.

Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Presidency University (~1913–1917), University of Calcutta (~1917–1919), and University of Allahabad. He taught Sanskrit at Allahabad (~1924–1956) and served at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1957–1968).

Buddhist studies scholar K. L. Dhammajoti earned an M.A. at the University of Kelaniya under Yin Shun and Y. Karunadasa. He held posts at the University of Calgary (2002), Kelaniya, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and HKU (~2004–2014).

Kuladasa Karunadasa Jayatilleke specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Cambridge under Ludwig Wittgenstein (1945–1948) and under Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera, later serving as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon (attested 1963).

Kumataro Kawada specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Tokyo Imperial University, he held posts at Tokyo University of Literature and Science (~1930–1949), University of Tokyo (~1950–1960), Komazawa University (~1960–1970), and Japan Women's University.

Kun Chang was a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at Tsinghua University (~1936–1940) and under Franklin Edgerton (~1948–1955), subsequently holding posts at the University of Washington (~1951–1963) and UC Berkeley (~1963–1987).

Kunio Harikai is an Indologist and philosopher who completed his BA and PhD degrees at Kyushu University, studying under Seiren Matsunami and Shoren Ihara. He served as Associate Professor at Saga Medical School (~1978–1993).

Kuno Lorenz is a philosopher who studied at the University of Kiel (~1956–1961). He held academic posts at the University of Hamburg (~1970–1974) and Saarland University, where he was a professor (attested 2010).

Philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar Kuntala Bhattacharya completed her PhD at Jadavpur University (attested 2009), supervised by Amita Chatterjee, Shyamapada Misra, and Prabal Kumar Sen. She held a post at Rabindra Bharati University (attested 2009).

Kurt A. Behrendt works in art history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his PhD at UCLA (~1990–1997) and was Assistant Curator of Asian Art at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (~2006).
Kurt Andrew Johnson is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of York in 2010 under the supervision of Jane Moody.

Philosopher Kurt Huber attended Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium and studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1913–1917). He subsequently held an academic post at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from around 1920 to 1943.

Kurt Tropper works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna (-2001) under Ernst Steinkellner, Michael Torsten Much, and Tashi Geisler, later holding posts at Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Kurtis R. Schaeffer studies Tibetology and Buddhism. He earned an MA at the University of Washington and studied at Harvard under Leonard van der Kuijp. He held posts at the University of Alabama (attested 2006) and University of Virginia (~2005).
Kurunegoda Piyatissa was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as the head of the New York Buddhist Vihara (attested 1998, 2009).

Kwangsoo Park is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Iowa and a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later serving as a professor at Wonkwang University (attested 2020).

Kyo Kano is an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Keio University, Kyoto University, and the University of Vienna, later holding posts as an assistant at Kyoto University (attested 1989) and associate professor at Kobe Women's University (attested 2000).
